item.stem:
Ishita looks at the diagram. Straight lines $AB$ and $CD$ cross at $O$. The marked angle $\angle AOC$ is $72^{\circ}$, and $p$ labels the angle vertically opposite $\angle AOC$.

Which claim correctly gives the measure of $p$?

options.A: $p = 108^{\circ}$, treating an adjacent angle on a straight line as if it were the vertically opposite angle.
options.B: $p = 72^{\circ}$, because vertically opposite angles at the same intersection are equal.
options.C: $p = 72^{\circ}$, because the angles may be called opposite angles that must sum to $180^{\circ}$.
options.D: $p = 72^{\circ}$, only because $72$ is already printed near the crossing.
